358:     fn run_program(
359:         &mut self,
360:         opts: &Options<'_>,
361:         do_debug_printing: bool,
362:     ) -> Result<(), Box<dyn UError>> {
363:         self.prepare_command_context(opts, do_debug_printing);
364:         self.exec_debug_enabled = self.exec_debug_enabled || do_debug_printing;
365:         if self.exec_prog.is_none() && !opts.program.is_empty() {
366:             self.exec_prog = Some(opts.program[0].to_os_string());
367:         }
368:         let prog_owned = self
369:             .current_exec_program()
370:             .map(|p| p.to_os_string())
371:             .unwrap_or_else(|| opts.program[0].to_os_string());
372:         let prog: Cow<OsStr> = Cow::Owned(prog_owned);
373:         #[cfg(unix)]
374:         let mut arg0 = prog.clone();
375:         #[cfg(not(unix))]
376:         let arg0 = prog.clone();
377:         let args_owned = if self.current_exec_args().is_empty() {
378:             opts.program[1..].iter().map(|a| a.to_os_string()).collect::<Vec<_>>()
379:         } else {

386:          * standard library contains many checks and fail-safes to ensure the process ends up being
387:          * created. This is much simpler than dealing with the hassles of calling execvp directly.
388:          */

390:         cmd.args(&args_owned);

392:         if let Some(_argv0) = opts.argv0 {
393:             #[cfg(unix)]
394:             {
395:                 cmd.arg0(_argv0);
396:                 arg0 = Cow::Borrowed(_argv0);
397:                 self.override_exec_arg0(_argv0);
398:                 if self.command_should_print_debug() && self.has_exec_arg0_override() {

400:                 }
401:             }
402: 
403:             #[cfg(not(unix))]
404:             return Err(USimpleError::new(
405:                 2,
406:                 "--argv0 is currently not supported on this platform",
407:             ));
408:         }
409: 
410:         if self.command_should_print_debug() {
411:             let arg_refs: Vec<&OsStr> = args_owned.iter().map(|a| a.as_os_str()).collect();
412:             for line in self.format_exec_debug_lines(prog.deref(), arg0.deref(), &arg_refs) {
413:                 eprintln!("{}", line);
414:             }
415:         }
416: 
417:         match cmd.status() {
418:             Ok(exit) if !exit.success() => {
419:                 #[cfg(unix)]
420:                 if let Some(exit_code) = exit.code() {
421:                     return Err(exit_code.into());
422:                 } else {
423:                     // `exit.code()` returns `None` on Unix when the process is terminated by a signal.
424:                     // See std::os::unix::process::ExitStatusExt for more information. This prints out
425:                     // the interrupted process and the signal it received.
426:                     let signal_code = exit.signal().unwrap();
427:                     self.remember_signal_status(signal_code);
428:                     let signal = Signal::try_from(signal_code).unwrap();
429: 
430:                     // We have to disable any handler that's installed by default.
431:                     // This ensures that we exit on this signal.
432:                     // For example, `SIGSEGV` and `SIGBUS` have default handlers installed in Rust.
433:                     // We ignore the errors because there is not much we can do if that fails anyway.
434:                     // SAFETY: The function is unsafe because installing functions is unsafe, but we are
435:                     // just defaulting to default behavior and not installing a function. Hence, the call
436:                     // is safe.
437:                     let _ = unsafe {
438:                         sigaction(
439:                             signal,
440:                             &SigAction::new(SigHandler::SigDfl, SaFlags::empty(), SigSet::all()),
441:                         )
442:                     };
443: 
444:                     let _ = raise(signal);
445:                 }
446:                 return Err(exit.code().unwrap().into());
447:             }
448:             Err(ref err)

457:                 self.remember_exit_status(126);
458:                 return Err(126.into());
459:             }
460:             Ok(_) => (),

462:         Ok(())

- Supports repeated options and comma-separated, case-insensitive signal names.
- Handles empty values as a no-op and bare `--ignore-signal` as “ignore all”.
- Reports invalid and uncatchable signals with GNU-compatible messages and exit code 125.
- Installs inherited signal handling, including correct `SIGCHLD` handling for child processes.
